learning_goal: Trace one red cell from the placenta back to the placenta, name the three shunts and say what each one bypasses and why, explain why the best-oxygenated blood reaches the brain and the heart, describe what the first breath and the clamped cord change about pressure and resistance, list what each fetal vessel becomes in the adult, and use all of it to explain patent ductus arteriosus, duct-dependent lesions and persistent fetal circulation.

structures.name: Placenta
structures.label: Placenta — where gas exchange actually happens

structures.name: Umbilical vein
structures.label: Umbilical vein — the only truly oxygenated vessel
structures.narration: One umbilical vein leaves the placenta carrying blood at about eighty percent saturation — the highest anywhere in the fetus, and lower than any adult arterial value. Note the reversal that catches students out: in the cord the vein carries the oxygenated blood and the two arteries carry the deoxygenated. It enters the abdomen at the umbilicus and runs up in the free edge of the falciform ligament, which is exactly where you will find its adult remnant.

structures.name: Ductus venosus
structures.label: Ductus venosus — shunt one, past the liver
structures.narration: Most of that blood does not enter the hepatic sinusoids. The ductus venosus carries roughly half of it straight from the umbilical vein into the inferior vena cava, so the liver — an organ the fetus does not need for detoxification while the mother's liver is available — does not slow down the delivery of oxygen. The rest perfuses the liver itself and rejoins by the hepatic veins.

structures.name: Inferior vena cava
structures.label: Inferior vena cava — the well-oxygenated stream
structures.narration: The shunted blood mixes with venous return from the lower body and reaches the right atrium at about seventy percent saturation. It arrives as a stream rather than a swirl — this is the single most important idea in the whole topic, because the fetus has no way to separate oxygenated from deoxygenated blood except by keeping the two streams apart as they cross the right atrium.

structures.narration: The same vessel as the inferior vena cava, cut at both ends at a landmark: the hepatic venous confluence below and the caval opening of the diaphragm above. It is here so that the beat about the ductus venosus can show what the duct empties into without putting six units of cava along that beat’s own line of sight — viz3d frames on the bounding box, so cranial reach is distance. It is never shown in the same frame as the whole cava.

structures.label: Superior vena cava — the poorly oxygenated stream
structures.narration: Blood returning from the head and upper limbs enters the right atrium from above, is directed downwards across the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, and barely mixes with the inferior caval stream at all. Two streams, two destinations, in the same chamber.

structures.narration: The free lower edge of the septum secundum overhangs the mouth of the inferior vena cava as a ledge called the crista dividens. It splits the incoming stream, sending most of it straight through the foramen ovale into the left atrium and letting the remainder turn down into the right ventricle. The fetus does not mix and then divide; it aims.

structures.label: Foramen ovale — shunt two, past the lungs and the right heart
structures.narration: Because right atrial pressure exceeds left, the thin septum primum is pushed aside and blood crosses right to left through the foramen ovale. The best-oxygenated blood in the body therefore arrives in the left atrium without ever passing through the lungs or the right ventricle.

views.title: Two resistances decide everything
views.narration:
Start with two numbers rather than a diagram. Pulmonary vascular resistance is very high because the lungs are fluid-filled and their vessels are constricted. Systemic vascular resistance is very low because the placenta is an enormous low-resistance bed. Blood goes where resistance is least, so it avoids the lungs and heads for the placenta, and three shunts exist to let it do that — one past the liver, one past the right heart, one past the lungs. Learn the two resistances and the three shunts stop being a list to memorise.

The fetus breathes through the placenta, not the lungs. The lungs are full of fluid and their vessels are clamped tight, so pulmonary resistance is very high, while the placenta is a huge low-resistance bed that keeps systemic resistance low. Blood therefore wants to go anywhere except the lungs. Three shunts are built to let it: one past the liver, one past the right side of the heart, and one past the lungs. Every fetal peculiarity follows from those two resistances and those three shunts.

views.title: Follow one red cell from the placenta
views.narration: Now walk the whole route once, out loud. Umbilical vein at eighty percent, the highest in the body. Ductus venosus past the liver into the inferior vena cava. Into the right atrium at about seventy percent, aimed by the crista dividens through the foramen ovale into the left atrium. Left ventricle, ascending aorta, coronaries and carotids — the brain and the heart get the best of it. Meanwhile the superior caval stream crosses into the right ventricle, meets a shut pulmonary bed and crosses the ductus arteriosus into the descending aorta below the left subclavian. Then out along the two umbilical arteries to the placenta to start again. Say that route until it is automatic; most of the marks in this topic are in it.

views.title: Past the liver — the ductus venosus
views.narration: The first shunt, on its own and close enough to see. Umbilical venous blood arrives at about eighty percent saturation — the highest anywhere in the fetus — and the liver is not yet doing the work it will do after birth, so roughly half of it is sent straight past through the ductus venosus into the inferior vena cava. The rest goes through the portal sinus into the liver itself and leaves by the hepatic veins, and the two streams meet again in the inferior cava. That is why the blood arriving at the right atrium is better oxygenated than any other venous blood in the body: most of it never went through an organ.

The inferior caval stream is well oxygenated and the superior caval stream is not, and they cross the same chamber without properly mixing — the inferior one aimed by the crista dividens at the foramen ovale, the superior one turning down to the tricuspid orifice. The chamber wall is drawn translucent so the crossing inside it can be seen.

views.title: Two events at birth, every closure follows
views.narration:
Two events, and you can derive the rest. The lungs open, so pulmonary resistance falls, pulmonary flow rises and left atrial pressure goes up. The cord is clamped, so systemic resistance rises and right atrial pressure comes down. Left now exceeds right, the flap valve is pressed shut and the foramen ovale closes functionally in minutes. Rising oxygen and the loss of placental prostaglandin constrict the ductus arteriosus over ten to fifteen hours. Umbilical flow stops, so the ductus venosus closes. Then name what each becomes: ligamentum teres, ligamentum venosum, fossa ovalis, ligamentum arteriosum, medial umbilical ligaments — and remember the superior vesical arteries stay open and keep working.

The lungs inflate, the fluid is cleared and alveolar oxygen dilates the pulmonary vessels. Pulmonary vascular resistance collapses, pulmonary blood flow increases many times over, and all that blood returns to the left atrium, whose pressure now rises.

Clamping the cord removes the largest low-resistance bed in the circulation, so systemic resistance jumps. At the same time the umbilical venous return stops, so right atrial pressure falls. Two changes, one result: left atrial pressure now exceeds right for the first time, and it stays that way for life.

The foramen ovale shuts because the pressures reversed and the septum primum is pressed against the septum secundum — no tissue has to grow for that, only for permanent fusion over the following months. The ductus arteriosus constricts within about ten to fifteen hours as oxygen tension rises, placental prostaglandin E2 disappears and bradykinin acts on its muscular wall, and it is anatomically sealed within two to three weeks. The ductus venosus closes once umbilical flow stops. Distinguish functional closure, which happens in hours, from anatomical closure, which takes weeks — that distinction is the whole reason a duct can be reopened with a drug.

views.title: The flap is pressed shut
views.narration: Same moment, at the septum, seen from the right — the side a student meets the fossa from. Left atrial pressure has now overtaken right, and the septum primum flap — hinged on the caudal rim of the foramen with its free edge cranial — is held against the septum secundum. Nothing has grown and nothing has torn: the leaf lies flat because the gradient it hung open on has reversed. The arrow still crossing the septum is a tenth of the fetal one by drawn area, because a residual shunt is not the same as no shunt: permanent fusion takes months, which is why a quarter of adults keep a probe-patent foramen and why this closure is called functional rather than anatomical.

views.title: Fifteen minutes old — the duct turns round
views.narration: Watch the arrows in the duct, and nothing else. A quarter of an hour ago they pointed from the pulmonary trunk into the aorta, because the lungs were the hard way round. Now they point from the aorta into the pulmonary trunk. Nothing was rebuilt and no valve moved: the two resistances swapped places, and the blood went the way that was easier, which is the only thing blood has ever done. A normal newborn shunts a little left to right across a duct that is still closing, for the ten to fifteen hours it takes to shut. Hold on to this frame, because a duct that fails to shut is stuck here — and the murmur, the bounding pulses and the drug that treats it all follow from an arrow pointing this way instead of that way.

views.narration: Five pairs to know cold — the three below the diaphragm first. Umbilical vein becomes the ligamentum teres hepatis in the free edge of the falciform ligament. Ductus venosus becomes the ligamentum venosum. The distal umbilical arteries become the medial umbilical ligaments while their proximal parts stay open as the superior vesical arteries — the only fetal vessel on this list that keeps a job.

views.narration: Foramen ovale becomes the fossa ovalis, and the free lower edge of the septum secundum — the crista dividens that aimed the inferior stream — becomes its limbus. This is the view from the right, because the fossa is a right atrial feature: a shallow dimple with a raised crescent along the margin the crista occupied. Ductus arteriosus becomes the ligamentum arteriosum, and the left recurrent laryngeal nerve stays hooked under it for life.

views.title: When the duct stays open — and when it must not close
views.narration:
The duct can be wrong in either direction. Left open when it should have shut, the reversed gradient makes it shunt left to right — a continuous machinery murmur, bounding pulses, and a prostaglandin inhibitor to close it. But in a duct-dependent lesion it is the only connection the baby has, and closing it causes collapse on day two or three; there prostaglandin E1 keeps it open until surgery. The third failure is on the lung side: if pulmonary resistance never falls, the shunts keep running right to left and the newborn stays blue, with hypoxia and acidosis making the constriction worse. Finish every question the same way — trace the blood, name the shunt and the gradient, apply the two birth events, then name the remnant.

If the duct stays open after birth the pressure gradient has reversed, so flow now runs from aorta to pulmonary trunk — left to right, through both systole and diastole. That is the continuous machinery murmur below the left clavicle, with bounding pulses and a wide pulse pressure. It is common in premature babies and classically associated with congenital rubella. Because prostaglandin holds the duct open, a prostaglandin synthesis inhibitor such as indomethacin or ibuprofen closes it.

Reverse the logic and you have the most useful fact in neonatal cardiology. In some malformations the only route between the two circulations is the duct itself — transposition, pulmonary atresia, critical coarctation, hypoplastic left heart. Those babies are stable while the duct is open and collapse in the first days of life as it closes. Prostaglandin E1 keeps it open and buys time for surgery. A newborn who is well at birth and becomes blue or shocked on day two or three, especially with absent femoral pulses, is a duct closing on a lesion that needed it.

views.title: When the lung side fails — persistent fetal circulation
views.narration:
This is six weeks old with the lung side of the transition never completed. The duct is still the calibre it had before birth, and the arrows in it still run right to left — away from the lung, into the systemic circulation — which is why this baby is blue while the previous frame’s baby is pink and overloaded. The foramen is shunting the same way at the same moment, and the next frame shows it. Compare the duct here with the duct in the frame before: the same vessel, the same age, shunting the other way.

The transition can also fail on the lung side. If pulmonary vascular resistance does not fall — after meconium aspiration, birth asphyxia, sepsis or with hypoplastic lungs — the foramen ovale and duct keep shunting right to left and the baby stays hypoxic. Hypoxia and acidosis constrict the pulmonary vessels further, so the failure feeds itself. This is why the transition is described as a circulation that must be actively completed rather than a switch that flips at delivery.

views.title: Persistent fetal circulation — the foramen is shunting too
views.narration:
Same baby, the same instant, at the atrial septum. The arrows through the foramen still run right to left — away from the lung, into the systemic circulation — which is why this baby is blue. The flap has not been pressed shut, because the pressure that shuts it never arrived: left atrial pressure overtakes right only once the lungs open and pulmonary resistance falls, and here it has not. So both shunts are still running, which is the whole of the lesion — and it is why hypoxia and acidosis make it worse, since each constricts the pulmonary vessels further and holds the gradient where it is.

Note what is NOT drawn here. The crista dividens is still aiming the inferior caval stream at the foramen exactly as it did before birth. Nothing has grown, nothing has torn and nothing has been re-plumbed: this is the fetal arrangement, unchanged, in a baby who is six weeks old.

gaps: THE ADAPTER PAINTS A STRUCTURE ONE COLOUR, SO THE MODEL'S SOLVED SATURATION DOES NOT REACH A STUDENT. viz3d.js merges every mesh carrying a key into one geometry and gives it one MeshStandardMaterial coloured from the SCENE's color field (or the model's LAYERS palette) - the material the model built, which carries the solved oxygen saturation at that t, is discarded. In a direct render the whole picture recolours as the transition proceeds, and the umbilical vein, inferior cava, ascending aorta, descending aorta and umbilical artery come out in that order by measured pixel warmth (120.8, 87.5, 75.2, 53.3, 52.0 red-minus-blue). In the player they are flat anatomical colours. The scene keeps the original author's colours, which at least carry the vein-artery reversal in the cord, and nothing is shown that is WRONG - but the single best thing this model does is currently invisible in the app. The fix is an engine change and belongs on its own queue item: let the adapter keep the built mesh's own colour when the scene declares none.

THE FLOW LAYER IS ONE STRUCTURE COVERING EVERY VESSEL'S ARROWS, so a view that hides a vessel leaves its arrows hanging in mid air. Measured, not predicted: beats 3 and 4 were first authored isolating a region with the flow layer on, and rendered as a cloud of loose gold cones. The rule applied here is that a view either shows the whole circuit and may show flow, or isolates a region and must not. The better fix is per-vessel marker keys in the model so a view can show exactly the arrows of the vessels it is showing. RESOLVED 2026-09-30 (round 3): FLOW_KEY_OF/FLOW_KEYS partition the markers and the three shunts each carry their own key (flow_ductus_venosus, flow_foramen_ovale, flow_ductus_arteriosus), so an isolating beat can now show exactly its own arrows. It cost three structures, not the twenty-odd feared here. The monolithic `flow` key remains for the whole-circuit beats and no longer carries the duct. [REVIEW 2026-09-30: this gap still described the fix as undone two rounds after it was built.]

THE MODEL AGREES WITH THE NARRATION, NOT WITH THE LITERATURE, ON ONE NUMBER, and it is flagged rather than resolved. The ductus venosus narration says it carries 'roughly half' of umbilical venous flow, and the model uses 0.50 so the picture agrees with the words a student is reading. Human fetal MRI in late gestation puts it nearer 0.30. Whoever reviews this should decide which one the corpus teaches; the build task is not the right place to overrule the narration silently. REVIEWER'S DECISION 2026-09-30, so this stops recurring: KEEP 0.50. This corpus is exam-oriented and the standard texts a student is marked against teach 'roughly half'; the narration says 'roughly half'; and the model agreeing with the words on screen is worth more here than agreeing with late-gestation MRI. The 0.30 figure stays recorded in this gap as the better physiological number and as the reason a reader may see a discrepancy. This is a reviewer's call on an editorial question the build task correctly refused to make silently, and Frank can overrule it; it is no longer an open question for either task, and neither should raise it again without new reason.

THE INFERIOR VENA CAVA IS MODELLED AS ONE WELL-MIXED STREAM, and it should probably be two. Because the ductus venosus stream at 0.80 is a large part of it, holding the mixed inferior caval saturation at the narration's stated 0.70 forces the lower body's oxygen extraction down to about a tenth of the whole body's, which is not a fetus. In life the ductus venosus stream and the lower-body stream do not mix before the crista dividens - which is the same streaming the crista then exploits - so the 0.70 belongs to a stream, not to a mixture. This does not change any relation the scene asserts; it changes how the upper-to-lower extraction split is apportioned inside the solve.

THE CORONARY ARTERIES ARE NOT BUILT. Beat 6 teaches that the ascending aorta’s "first branches are the coronaries and then the vessels to the head and upper limbs", and this model builds no coronary geometry at all - head_neck_vessels are the first branches a student actually sees leave the arch. Nothing wrong is drawn and the narration is correct; the claim is simply unsupported by the picture. Declared here 2026-09-30 against review finding R1-OPEN-2 (round 1, 2026-09-21), which is precisely what gaps[] is for. The coronaries carry no shunt and no saturation this scene teaches, so building them would add two vessels and no lesson; the honest fix is this line. gross__heart-pericardium__coronary-arteries-cardiac-veins is where they are taught and has its own scene.

THE NEWBORN PREDUCTAL SATURATION CURVE DISAGREES WITH THE PUBLISHED ONE, AND IT IS NOT A MIS-TUNED PARAMETER - IT IS PROVEN UNREACHABLE IN THIS NETWORK. Round 1 finding R1-OPEN-4 said the model reads 0.543 / 0.962 / 0.976 at 1, 5 and 10 minutes against published 0.60-0.65 / 0.80-0.85 / 0.85-0.95, and asked for the number to be settled. Round 2 measured the model’s aoa saturation as a function of the IMPOSED aeration fraction at each checkpoint (11 values, 0.01-0.99, by driving EVENTS.breath to a chosen value at that instant). Reading the published bands back through that response: one minute needs the lung 0.42-0.49 aerated and two minutes needs it 0.385-0.411 aerated. The second interval lies BELOW the first, and aeration is monotone, so no aeration profile of any shape can satisfy both - not one logistic, not two phases, not anything. A 70-point sweep of single-logistic ranges agrees from the other side: the best puts 4 of 6 checkpoints in band and drags one minute to 0.263. THE CAUSE: the published curve rises only 0.05 between one and two minutes because oxygenating a newborn means filling an oxygen STORE - a whole circulating volume, plus progressive alveolar recruitment - and a store is capacitive. This is a steady-state resistive network with instantaneous mixing, so its arterial saturation tracks aeration immediately and has no capacity to buffer a nadir. THE REMEDY is a transit/equilibration term, which is a different model and a queue item of its own, not a constant to bend here. Acceptance row R now asserts the shape this model CAN claim - a nadir below the fetal value within two minutes of the clamp, monotone rise from it, plateau above 0.97 by six weeks - and report.json carries agrees_with_published:false beside the numbers so they cannot be quoted as agreement. No view renders the curve.

THE PLAYER VISIBILITY WALK NOW PASSES ON ALL THIRTEEN BEATS. CORRECTED 2026-09-30 BY THE REVIEW TASK - this entry previously read 'THE PLAYER VISIBILITY WALK FAILS ON ALL NINE BEATS' and was left in place through round 3, which built the beats that fixed it. As committed, measure-scene-visibility.mjs (three.js r128; thresholds any >= 0.02%, pointed-at >= 0.3%, subject >= 8% of frame) reports 13 beats, 0 failures, EVERY STRUCTURE A BEAT DRAWS OR POINTS AT IS SEEABLE. Re-run by the reviewer rather than taken from the build log. WHAT ROUND 2 ESTABLISHED ABOUT THE CAUSE, kept because it is still the best account of why the shunts are hard to show: (1) OPACITY HELPS AND IS NOT ENOUGH - placenta 0.42, liver 0.38, lungs 0.34, the four chambers 0.42 and the septum 0.55 moved every shunt up and closed none. (2) IT IS OCCLUSION BY THE GREAT VESSELS, NOT SCALE - the duct at 21.8% of the framed extent still drew 0.058%. (3) CAMERA DIRECTION IS THE BIGGEST SINGLE LEVER for a whole-circuit frame, and was still 3.4x short. (4) THE MONOLITHIC FLOW LAYER BLOCKED THE OBVIOUS REMEDY; per-vessel flow keys were the enabling fix and were built in round 3. WHAT ACTUALLY WORKED, from the round-3 probes: A SUPERIOR CAMERA ON A TIGHT STRUCTURE SET CLEARS EVERY SHUNT, because these are long thin tubes and a camera that fits the bounding box of a set spread over the whole fetus fills that box with empty space. AND THE COST OF THAT REMEDY, WHICH IS THE REVIEWER'S OPEN FINDING R2-OPEN-1 (see the queue): on BEAT 4 the superior camera looks straight down the shared axis of the superior and inferior venae cavae, so the SVC renders as a featureless disc at 10.595% and occludes the IVC to 0.046%. The beat exists to compare those two streams. The camera that passes the subject floor is the one camera that destroys the comparison.

BEAT 4 FAILS THE 8% SUBJECT FLOOR AND IS WAIVED ON A MEASURED ARGUMENT, not a lowered threshold. Round 4, closing review finding R2-OPEN-1. The beat's subject is the two venae cavae - two long thin tubes running the length of the trunk - and the camera fits their bounding box, which is 9.31% filled. No camera and no subject choice satisfies both the teaching and the floor: the full six-camera sweep is in the beat's visibility_waivers entry. The floor rewards exactly the camera that hides half the subject, which is review finding R2-STANDARDS-GAP-1 and is a change to measure-scene-visibility.mjs shared by ~150 scenes - proposed there, not landed here. WHAT DID CHANGE IN THE MODEL: the inferior and superior caval streams now carry their own flow keys (flow_ivc, flow_svc), so beat 4 can draw the two streams its narration points at without the whole circuit's cloud. Beats 2 and 7 show both keys as well, so the partition changed no frame but beat 4's - proved rather than asserted: every structure in beats 2 and 7 reproduces its pre-change percentage to three decimals and the three flow keys sum to the single old one exactly (beat 2: 1.008+0.217+0.122 = 1.347; beat 7: 0.551+0.194+0.129 = 0.874).

PERSISTENT FETAL CIRCULATION NOW HAS ITS FORAMEN, AS BEAT 14. Round 4, closing review finding R2-OPEN-2, which found beat 13 narrating ‘the arrows in it and through the foramen still run right to left’ over a frame containing no foramen. The reviewer left the choice of fix to the author and named the cost of each: adding the foramen to beat 13 breaks the controlled comparison beats 12 and 13 exist to make - they are deliberately identical but for the duct, and beat 13's own narration leans on that - while giving PFC a second frame does not. THE VISIBILITY WALK WAS MIS-MEASURING THIS SCENE, AND EVERY OTHER SCENE PAST 32 STRUCTURES. Found by round 4 and FIXED IN THE TOOL, viz-training/tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs. The structure id was written into the red channel alone as id*8, so the 33rd structure onward clamped to 255 and every one of them decoded as the 32nd. Consequences here, all now corrected: pfc_duct and pfc_flow read 0.000 and were passing only on the through-the-wall rescue (they are 0.410 and 0.522); pda_flow's pixels were being added to pda_duct, which is why pda_duct read 0.905 and now reads 0.571 + 0.334 = 0.905 exactly; and `midline` collapsed to 0.000 the moment two structures were inserted ahead of it, which is how the bug was found. REVIEW ROUND 2 CAME WITHIN ONE STEP OF THIS and was right not to guess: it recorded pfc_duct as ‘~10x worse than ductus_arteriosus’ and declined to call it a scene defect because ‘scene vs +pfc variant vs the harness's variant-ref handling has not been isolated’. It was the harness. The id is now split across two channels; ids 1-32 encode byte-identically, so no scene at or under 32 structures can be re-graded, and that was verified over all 1023 ids on the pinned renderer rather than argued from the arithmetic. Four procedural scenes this tool grades carry more than 32 structures - cardiac-looping at 51, heart-external at 42, coronary-arteries-cardiac-veins at 35, and this one - and THEIR PAST WALK RESULTS SHOULD BE TREATED AS UNRELIABLE UNTIL RE-RUN. This run did not re-run them: three of the four are other queue items and re-grading them is not this item's to do.

THE DUCT ARROWS IN BEAT 9 WERE POINTING THE FETAL WAY, IN THE ONE BEAT WRITTEN TO SHOW THEM REVERSE. FOUND AND FIXED BY REVIEW ROUND 3, 2026-09-30. The structure flow_ductus_arteriosus carried the ref 'fetal-circulation#flow_ductus_arteriosus@0'. viz3d.js atStage() returns null for a pinned ref (`if (!r || r.tPinned) return null`, viz3d.js:561) and stageable() reports it unstageable, so SET_STAGE CANNOT restage a pinned structure - the round-3 build note claiming 'SET_STAGE re-pins per view so the pin changes no picture' is false against the very lines it asked a reviewer to check, and the same note's separate claim that the pin merely changes a marker's SIZE is what that error looked like from the inside. markerCones() orients every cone by the SIGN of the solved flow (`const dir = qSigned >= 0 ? 1 : -1`, models3d/fetal-circulation.js:995). The solved duct flow is da=+0.5800 at t=0 and da=-0.1639 at beat 9's t=0.25. So beat 9 - 'Fifteen minutes old, the duct turns round', whose narration is 'A quarter of an hour ago they pointed from the pulmonary trunk into the aorta ... Now they point from the aorta into the pulmonary trunk' - was drawing the t=0 arrows, pointing the fetal way, at 3.5x the correct magnitude (len scales with min(1, mag/0.60): 3.347 against 2.237). MEASURED CONSEQUENCE beyond direction: the oversized markers were covering the duct they annotate - repinned to @0.25, ductus_arteriosus goes 0.383% to 0.559% of frame and flow_ductus_arteriosus 0.509% to 0.291%, in a frame identical in every other respect. FIXED as @0.25 rather than by removing the pin, because the build note's reason for pinning at all - an unpinned flow ref resolves reason:none at a t where the model emits no marker, which the player shows a student as 'there is no model of this structure' - is sound, and beat 9 is the only view that uses this key. HOW IT SURVIVED: validate-scenes passes (the ref resolves); the visibility walk passes (it counts pixels, not direction); acceptance row L and the 'duct reversal 76.1% of lit pixels' check both measure the MODEL at two values of t, where the reversal is real, and never the beat. NOTHING IN THE CHAIN ASKS WHETHER A BEAT'S ARROWS POINT THE WAY ITS NARRATION SAYS. This is the third defect in this scene found by asking 'how did it pass?' rather than 'did it pass?'.

CLOSED ROUND 5 - BEAT 3 NOW SHOWS WHAT THE DUCT EMPTIES INTO, as a TERMINAL CAVA on its own key. Review finding R3-OPEN-1. The reviewer measured the cost of the obvious fix through the real tool and left the authoring call: adding the whole `ivc` collapses the beat's own highlighted ductus venosus from 1.258 to 0.072 per cent. The reason is in viz3d's distanceForBox: it ADDS the subject box's half-extent along the view direction to the camera distance, so from beat 3's superior camera every unit of cranial reach is a unit of standing back. So the second of the reviewer's two options was taken - a short segment as its own key - and it is cut at a LANDMARK AT BOTH ENDS, the hepatic venous confluence below and the caval opening of the diaphragm above, which is the segment a student is taught anyway. MEASURED, three cuts walked through the real tool: to the right atrium (y=1.95) ductus_venosus 0.085; caudal of the confluence (y=-0.95) 0.087; at the confluence to the diaphragm (y=-0.40 to 0.15) 0.162 on the id-pick and 0.607 through the liver, with ivc_terminal itself at 2.361 and the beat's subject back up to 22.66%. The duct is still read through the liver it runs inside, which it always was - it is intrahepatic - and the beat passes. `ivc_terminal` is never shown in the same frame as `ivc`; its geometry is cut out of GEO.ivc itself rather than written out again, so the two cannot disagree about where the cava is.

CLOSED ROUND 5, BUT NOT THE WAY THE FINDING PROPOSED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS A FINDING ABOUT THE ENGINE. Review finding R3-OPEN-2 recommended adding CROSS_SECTION to beat 4, on the ground that 'viz3d.js:1912 implements CROSS_SECTION as a clip plane, so the op is available and the adapter supports it'. Line 1912 does record the clip. LINE 2438 IS WHERE IT IS APPLIED, and it reads `m.material.clippingPlanes = (clipping && !isTaught(s)) ? [clipPlane] : null`, with isTaught(s) at :167 returning `s.role !== 'context'`. SO CROSS_SECTION CUTS ONLY SCAFFOLDING. In this scene 41 of 42 structures are role 'part' and the only 'context' one is `midline`: a CROSS_SECTION on beat 4 would cut the median-plane trace and nothing else, and could not cut the right atrium at any offset. Cutting the atrium would mean demoting it to 'context', which takes it out of the student's parts list - a worse defect than the one being fixed. This is NOT proposed as an engine change here: the gating is deliberate (a cross-section that sliced the taught subject would be wrong in most of the 150 scenes) and changing it is shared-tooling work for a round that owns it. WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD IS THE SUBSTANCE OF THE FINDING - 'the frame shows two streams arriving at the chamber and never crossing it'. The two streams now CROSS, as geometry: models3d/fetal-circulation.js builds GEO.stream_ivc and GEO.stream_svc, each from its own caval mouth to its own destination - the septum for the inferior stream, which the crista dividens aims at the foramen, and the tricuspid orifice for the superior - carrying F.fo and F.svc, so the crossing is drawn only while something crosses and disappears at t=1 because the arithmetic stops it. Acceptance row W measures it: the chords pass within one stream width (0.313 against 0.400) at a point 0.334 of the way out of the right atrial ellipsoid, and not at either chord's end. The narration's opening was rewritten from 'Cut across the right atrium' to 'Look into the right atrium and follow the two streams across it', and says that the wall is translucent - which is what the player actually draws, the atrium being authored at opacity 0.42. THE HONEST LIMIT: measure-scene-visibility's id-pick pass replaces every material with an opaque one, so the intra-atrial markers are behind the atrial wall on that pass and beat 4's flow_ivc/flow_svc numbers (1.201 / 0.353) count only the extra-atrial markers, unchanged from round 4. The crossing is proved by row W and by the render, not by the walk.

CLOSED ROUND 5 - THE FORAMEN MARKER NOW CARRIES ITS MAGNITUDE IN BOTH DIMENSIONS, and the fix needed a second half the finding did not name. Review finding R3-OPEN-3. The marker takes markerCones' two rules instead of fixed extents: LENGTH by magLaw, now a named function both markers read so there is one copy of the rule, normalised by the FETAL shunt; WIDTH by the aperture the flap leaves, `GEO.septum.rIn * 1.32 * sin(ang)`, which is markerCones' own 'width is fixed to the vessel's CURRENT calibre' applied to the vessel this marker passes through. MEASURED: fetal w 0.150 l 0.640 (byte-for-byte the marker this model has always drawn - the fix is not a quietly smaller arrow everywhere), at beat 8's own t w 0.021 l 0.475, drawn area 10.5% of fetal. In the player: beat 8's flow_foramen_ovale 1.401% of frame to 0.110%, against a foramen_ovale at 4.692% - it was 3.8x the flap it passes through and is now a fortieth of it. Acceptance row V asserts both dimensions fall AND that the area clears FLOORS.marker, with two negative cases: the fetal dimensions restored (the defect itself) and both dimensions shrunk by one per cent (which a monotonicity test alone would pass). THE SECOND HALF, and it is why the review's own measurement said unpinning changes nothing: the scene's ref was `#flow_foramen_ovale@0`, and viz3d cannot restage a pinned ref, so beat 8 at t=0.0998 was drawing the model at t=0. That was harmless while the geometry did not depend on t and became load-bearing the moment it did - the model fix would have reached beat 5 and not beat 8. FIXED BY MINTING A SECOND KEY, not by unpinning - and the unpinned version was tried first and rejected on a measurement: with `#flow_foramen_ovale` and no @t the adapter's default is t=1 (viz3d.js:480), where the model emits no marker, so check 5 of render-fetal-circulation.mjs reported flow_foramen_ovale=none - the 'there is no model of this structure' lie the pin existed to prevent. So beat 5 keeps `@0` and beat 8 takes `flow_foramen_ovale_residual`, the same model part pinned `@0.0998`. That is the pattern pda_duct and pfc_duct already use on the ductus arteriosus, and it is the rule the new check states: two beats needing one part at two values of t need two keys. Found not by reading the scene but by a new check - see gaps[26].

CLOSED ROUND 5 - BOTH REMNANT BEATS NOW CLEAR THE POINTED-AT FLOOR ON THE HONEST ID-PICK PASS, with no through-the-wall rescue. THE UMBILICAL VEIN AND ARTERIES ARE STILL DRAWN OUT TO THE PLACENTA AT t=1, AT REMNANT CALIBRE - not just after birth (gaps[9] covers the beats hiding them) but on the beat that is ABOUT the remnants. The ligamentum teres is the INTRA-ABDOMINAL remnant, from the umbilicus to the liver; the cord beyond the umbilicus is cut and gone. Beat 10 therefore draws five cords spanning from the liver to where the placenta was, which is what makes its subject 4.88% of the frame - the framing waiver's argument is true but it is true about a span that should be shorter. THE FIX IS THE ONE THE UMBILICAL ARTERIES ALREADY HAVE: calibre() gives them an ALONG-VESSEL taper so the proximal part stays open as the superior vesical while the distal part becomes a thread. The umbilical VEIN needs the same treatment with the cut at the umbilicus, and the cord spans (uacord_L, uacord_R, and the placental end of GEO.umbilical_vein) should go to zero calibre rather than to REMNANT. NOT DONE THIS ROUND: it moves the picture in beats 1, 2, 7 and 10 and is a separate measured change, not a rider on four findings. Recorded here with its own argument so the next round can take it rather than rediscover it.

THE LIMBUS IS DRAWN ON THE CAUDAL RIM, WHICH IS WHERE THIS MODEL'S CRISTA DIVIDENS IS AND NOT WHERE THE ADULT LIMBUS IS MOST PROMINENT. The model builds crista_dividens as a crescent on the CAUDAL rim of the foramen, and its own comment gives the reason: that is the side the inferior caval stream arrives on, and drawn anywhere else it would be decorative. Beat 11 then identifies that crescent as the limbus fossae ovalis, which is the standard teaching line - the limbus IS the free edge of the septum secundum. But in the adult the limbus is most marked SUPERIORLY AND ANTERIORLY, and beat11.png shows the crescent below the fossa. FOUND BY LOOKING AT THE FRAME, round 5: the narration first written for this beat said 'along its upper and anterior margin', which the picture contradicted, and the words were changed to 'the margin the crista occupied' rather than the geometry, because the geometry is right for the fetal beats that the crista exists for (beats 5 and 8) and a crescent that moved between t=0 and t=1 would be asserting a migration that does not happen. THE HONEST FIX, not done here: give the septum a limbus of its own - a crescent on the cranial and ventral rim, appearing as the fossa forms - so the fetal crista and the adult limbus are two structures rather than one relabelled. That is a model change with its own acceptance row and it belongs to a round that owns it.

THE pfc VARIANT'S SATURATION FIELD HAS COLLAPSED ONTO THE 0.05 CLAMP, AND EVERY AUTOMATED CHECK CERTIFIES IT. Found by review round 4, 2026-09-30; ESCALATED as a decision, see ESCALATIONS.md. At t=1 in the pfc variant, seven of the fifteen solved saturations are EXACTLY the floor that saturations() applies with Math.max(0.05, ...) - hep, ivcLow, svc, ivc, ra, rv and pa all read 0.0500 - and the arterial values are computed from those clamped inputs: sat.aoa (preductal) 0.1972, sat.aod (postductal) 0.0558. A newborn at 20% preductal and 6% postductal is not a blue baby, it is an unsurvivable one; the teaching figures for PPHN are a preductal/postductal split in the 70-90% range with a gradient over ~10 points as the sign. The model has the gradient's SIGN right and its magnitudes meaningless. CAUSE, and it is structural rather than a mis-tuned constant: EXTRACT is solved once by bisection at t=0 against the fetal figures and memoised in _mix, then reused for every t and every variant. In pfc the lung takes 6% of combined output (derived.pulmonary_share 0.0605) and there is no placenta (flow.plac 0), so the only oxygen entering the body is 6% of output at 98% while a fetal-sized extraction keeps being subtracted; the subtraction goes negative, the clamp catches it, and the clamp injects oxygen conservation says is not there. The clamp is silently active in the HEALTHY path too - plain variant at t=1 has hep = 0.0500. THIS IS THE SAME LIMITATION AS gaps[13]: a steady-state resistive network with instantaneous mixing and fixed extraction cannot represent a circulation that is not in oxygen steady state, and that gap already recorded the remedy as a transit/equilibration term belonging to its own queue item. NOTHING A STUDENT SEES IS WRONG TODAY, by luck and not design: gaps[0] records that the adapter discards the model's solved saturation and paints flat scene colours, so the collapsed field never reaches the screen - and closing gaps[0] is itself an open queue item. HOW IT PASSED: every claim on the pfc beats is a one-sided bound on a SIGN. B13-BLUE is `pfc:sat.aod atMost 0.8` reading 0.0558, passing by a factor of fourteen while its prose asserts a magnitude nothing checks; B13-DA is `atLeast 0.3` reading 0.5571 while its prose says 'a third of the combined output'. check-beat-claims' +/-0.05 displacement cannot see this class, because a value wrong by an order of magnitude is still wrong after displacement. The claims are left UNCHANGED by this review on purpose: writing the correct band is the curriculum decision being escalated, and a reviewer who writes the band has made the call.

deferred_beats.title: How to answer any fetal circulation question
deferred_beats.narration: Four moves, in order. One: trace a red cell from placenta to placenta and name every vessel and shunt out loud — most marks are here. Two: at each shunt say what is being bypassed and which pressure difference drives the flow. Three: at birth, apply the two changes, lungs open and cord clamped, and let every closure follow from them. Four: name the remnant. Answer in that order and you never have to memorise the diagram as a picture.
deferred_beats.why_not_a_view: It is exam technique, not anatomy. There is no frame it could change: it describes the ORDER to say things in, and every structure it names is already shown by the view that teaches it. Rendered as a view it would be beat 2's frame with different words over it, which is what RENDER-STANDARD means by a beat that is text.
deferred_beats.belongs_in: the topic's revision notes, or as the scene's closing text panel — it is the best summary in this scene and it should not be a 3D beat
